verificationNotes: Routers start without IPv6 forwarding, routing protocols or static routes. Endpoints have fixed IPv6 addresses and interface-scoped link-local default routes; SLAAC and router advertisements are suppressed. IPv4 addresses are absent from all devices.

Published original classic IOS commands enable ipv6 unicast-routing, ipv6 router ospf 10, explicit 32-bit router IDs and per-interface ipv6 ospf 10 area 0. All commands are executed through IOSSession and rejected output fails validation.

The packet-driven engine exchanges OSPFv3 Hello/database packets, floods LSAs and computes SPF. Expected Full peers are bound to both device and local interface. LANs remain passive and advertise their /64 prefixes; no Hello is sent toward an endpoint.

Transit network type is point-to-point. Each transit end costs 10 except both direct R1/R3 ends at 5; LAN cost remains 1. Installed intra-area O routes must have AD 110, the intended link-local next hop, outgoing interface and metric 6 or 11.

Direct-link shutdown withdraws adjacency and selects metric 21 through R2 in both directions. Actual packet-event assertions and IPv6 traceroute prove alternate forwarding. Restoration recovers Full adjacency and metric 6. Loss on a physically up link waits for the default 40-second Dead interval.

Negative tests cover passive transit, one-sided area mismatch, Hello/Dead mismatch, removed LAN membership, wrong router ID, disabled IPv6 forwarding and wrong transit/passive-LAN costs. Alternate-path connectivity cannot substitute for the required live configuration or planned routes.

The completed reference earns six configuration/operational tasks after convergence; four real endpoint echo tests are required to complete all ten. Saved reload and startup reboot reconstruct protocol state and retain previously observed traffic, with fresh packets confirming current connectivity.

OSPF-interface criteria now accept a bounded optional ospf/ospfv3 selector. The default remains OSPFv2 for existing guides. Explicit compatibility tests cover legacy criteria, scoped peers, invalid selectors and normalized IPv6 addresses.

Fixed an existing show ipv6 ospf process-summary exception: IPv6 /64 and /128 prefixes bypass the IPv4 dotted-mask formatter. A regression case exercises the process and database displays on all three routers and confirms IPv4 Router-LSA masks and show ip ospf remain intact.

All six file:// browser scenarios run sequentially with isolated persistent profiles: light/dark at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels. They configure all routers through the real terminal, verify Full neighbors/passive LAN/received database, all four 3/3 traffic checks, direct/alternate metrics and traceroutes, failure-state reload, restored-state reload, completed reference and safe cancel/save-copy behavior.

Two permalink cases preserve the current origin, path and query string without replacing an open workspace; the Routing subsection displays eight labs. Seven generic catalog regression checks passed. No page errors or external application requests were observed.

The frozen offline HTML and all viewport copies match final root index.html and dist/index.html byte for byte. Desktop topology and light/dark mobile guide screenshots were visually reviewed. Existing terminal colors were checked in every new-lab browser scenario.
